questions.solution:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Present Continuous (Subject + is/am/are + V1 +ing + Object)

For example:

He said that he was checking the assignment. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I am checking the assignment." (Direct Speech)

In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, the verb in Direct speech is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

In the sentences beginning with the question word, the statement in the direct speech also begins with the same question word.

For example:

The teacher asked Jennie why she was late. (Indirect speech)

The teacher said to Jennie, "Why are you late?" (Direct speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

•'She' in the indirect speech is changed into 'you' in direct speech.

•'Asked' is changed into 'said to'.

•'Was' is changed into 'are'.

Also, inverted commas ("...") are placed in direct speech.

Option (a) is eliminated because the verb 'are' is not placed before the subject 'you'. Option (b) is eliminated because it is in Present Perfect Continuous tense. Option (c) is eliminated because it is in Past Continuous tense. Option (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The Principal said to Neha, "Where are you going after the graduation ceremony?"

questions.solution:
These kinds of sentences are called Optative Sentences.

Optative Sentences are usually prayers or wishes.

In these kinds of sentences, "said" in the Direct Speech is changed into "prayed", "wished", etc.

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

While changing from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech, the sentence is changed into its Assertive form i.e., "Subject + might/may + V1 + Object".

For example:

The father said to his son, "May God bless you!" (Direct Speech)

The father wished his son that God might bless him. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'wished'.

· 'May' is changed into 'might'.

· The possessive determiner 'your' is changed into 'my'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): The man wished me that my child might never know a hungry belly.

questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, a sentence is given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives choose the one which best expresses the sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.

The teacher said, “Kalidas is the Shakespeare of India”

options.text: The teacher said that Kalidas was the Shakespeare of India
options.html: The teacher said that Kalidas was the Shakespeare of India

options.text: The teacher said that Kalidas is the Shakespeare of India
options.html: The teacher said that Kalidas is the Shakespeare of India

options.text: The teacher said that Kalidas will be the Shakespeare of India
options.html: The teacher said that Kalidas will be the Shakespeare of India

options.text: The teacher said that Kalidas had been the Shakespeare of India
options.html: The teacher said that Kalidas had been the Shakespeare of India

questions.solution:
•We don't make changes in tenses of reported speech when reported speech expresses a Universal truth, fact, habits or Proverbs

•When the reporting verb is an assertive sentence we follow these steps-connector 'that' is used in place of commas. The tense and personal pronouns of reported speech remain unchanged for it's a universal statement, fact, proverbs or habits. Therefore, there will be no change in the 'Tense' of the 'Reported speech' of the above sentence

The correct answer is Option b) i.e. The teacher said that Kalidas is the Shakespeare of India.

questions.question: In the following question, a sentence is given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives choose the one which best expresses the sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech. The stranger said to me, "Please help me as I am lost."
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, a sentence is given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives choose the one which best expresses the sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.

The stranger said to me, "Please help me as I am lost."

options.text: The stranger requested me to help him as he is lost.
options.html: The stranger requested me to help him as he is lost.

options.text: The stranger requested me to help him as he has lost.
options.html: The stranger requested me to help him as he has lost.

options.text: The stranger requested me to help him as he was lost.
options.html: The stranger requested me to help him as he was lost.

options.text: The stranger requested me to help him as he were lost.
options.html: The stranger requested me to help him as he were lost.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option c)

Explanation:

•While changing the narration of an imperative sentence, we need to follow steps

•If the sentence is starting with "Please" and there is a request, we make the following changes-

•The reporting verb said is changed into requested or begged.

•Then 'to' infinitive with 1st form of the verb is used, followed the objective form of the pronoun. (Me-Him)

•The rest part is used as it is with the tense in past form.

Eventually, we will get the final sentence- "The stranger requested me to help him as he was lost."
